per_question.notes: 152 gives the Keyframe Velocity steps (Animation > Keyframe Velocity, in/out Speed + Influence, Easy Ease = 0 speed / 33.33%). Nothing in the corpus maps cubic-bezier x/y to influence/speed, gives Ctrl+Shift+K, or covers per-dimension eases (309 only shows the speed graph in px/s).

306 = Separate Dimensions, 308 = shaping value-graph handles, 316 = value graph for overshoots, but no hit makes the curve pass the target and settle. That recipe is 104 (settle key + middle key nudged in the value graph, right after 103 separates dims); it misses the top 5 but 'any' keyword mode returns it at rank 5.

No spatial-interpolation content anywhere: no Keyframe Interpolation > Spatial Linear, no 'Default Spatial Interpolation to Linear' preference, no Auto Bezier path overshoot. The hits cover roving keys and Exponential Scale; 310 only shows that motion-path handles are independent of speed.

43: Animate > Position + Opacity, keyframe Range Selector Offset, Advanced > Based On words. 166 (rank 2): Shape (Ramp/Smooth) and Ease High/Low. The link between stagger and selector duration is only implied, and the Randomize Order text is cut at the chunk end.

No VO-sync method anywhere (no audio waveform/LL, no word markers, no graphic-leads-the-word rule). Only Zammit's hero-word emphasis (46: null + slider + expression selector; 51: timing parts of a sentence) is relevant.

The corpus never animates Rectangle Path Size/Roundness. Hits use layer Scale with the anchor moved to an edge (100), which is the method the question rules out, and a 'maintain stroke width' expression whose code lives in a Google Doc, not the transcript (65). 98 only sets Size once.

59: Start/End/Offset with eased keys and stroke order for multi-path draws. 61 (rank 1): round cap, dot that follows the path end. 63/64: arrowhead rig. Trim Multiple Shapes Simultaneously/Individually is in doc 183 (not top-5).

The inertial-bounce code (amp/freq/decay, nearestKey, velocityAtTime, sin/exp) is split across 192 and 193 and is only usable because both came back at ranks 1-2. No tuning guidance and no Convert Expression to Keyframes.

192 has the basic sin/cos circular orbit. Nothing covers tilted-ellipse squash, depth-driven scale, or per-layer phase. Passing behind a subject only appears tangentially (114 matte trick, 199 3D fade by camera distance).
288 + 289: Enable DOF, Aperture/F-Stop/Blur Level, Set and Link Focus Distance to Layer (expression). No Z-spacing or renderer/performance note; doc 200 holds a focus-match expression.

Bricks gives a usable smooth-push recipe: nested 3D nulls, keyframe the next null before the previous move ends, easy ease + graph editor. 286 (rank 4) parents the camera to a null. Parallax from Z spacing is only in 82 (not top-5); no scale compensation.
292 + 291 answer it fully: switch needed in two places, enable blur inside the precomp or Collapse Transformations, Advanced tab settings, and the switch does not blur rendered footage.

95: RSMB with an animatable Blur Amount. 294: Timewarp/Pixel MB samples. 293: shutter angle/phase math. Missing: the 180 deg = 0.5 mapping, RSMB foreground/alpha handling for transparent footage, and fixes for vector artifacts.

The DG2 source is a 'what's new for DG1 users' tour (108/110): it names threshold, smoothness, saturation bias, gamma, exposure and quality but gives no starting values and no alpha-isolated source workflow. Middle chunk 109 (aberration, tint, tone mapping) ranks out. The Korenman stock-glow steps fill slots 2-4.

Korenman's duplicate > levels > blur > tint glow pass (299-301) is an adaptable isolated, tinted pass. But it composites with Add, which is exactly what fails on white, and nothing explains why glows vanish on light backgrounds.
No particle content at all (no Particular, CC Particle World or emitters). Retrieval returned glow tutorials with the same rank-only score as real answers.

121 punch zoom: scale 100->150 / 80->100, Motion Tile Mirror Edges, graph-editor ramp up and down, motion blur. 122 (rank 1) finishes the whip pan that starts at the end of 121. No frame durations; no Directional Blur.

113/112: the 2023 track-matte picker, invert, and why a matte beats a mask. 118: a mask-expand wipe with eased keys. The card part (animating Size/Roundness, shadowed edge) is missing, the same gap as n06.

208: 16 bpc reduces banding and AE dithers when it converts to 8-bpc output. No grain/noise anti-banding recipe or H.264 export advice; 124 has a generic noise adjustment layer in a transition context.

No cast/contact shadow, light wrap, or matte choke/edge match anywhere. Hits were Preserve Underlying Transparency and collapse-transformation docs. The Lumetri chunks (126-145) could only help the colour-match sub-point.

268/269/267: straight vs premultiplied, Guess, halo symptom, File > Interpret Footage > Main. The frame-rate half ('Conform to frame rate', 271-273) ranks out of the top 5; 'any' mode returns 271/273.

264: the Interpret Footage colour section matters mainly when no profile is embedded. No working-space settings, Preserve RGB, or ProRes gamma/601 info. 216 (linearize) and 218 (Compensate for Scene-referred Profiles, a common washed-out cause) exist but rank out.

321-325 + 231: continuous rasterization vs collapse, crisp scaling above 100%, comp-bounds removal, and side effects on effect point controls and 3D. Missing the 'build the precomp at the needed resolution' alternative.

235-238: full aerender syntax (-project/-comp/-s/-e, -RStemplate/-OMtemplate, -output, -mem_usage, -mfr). The flag table spans 235-239, so -continueOnMissingFootage (239) is cut off. No chunk-and-join guidance.

verdict.helps_today: Partly. 11/24 questions get an actionable answer and 9 a partial one, so the library is a useful second source for core AE mechanics: motion-blur switches, alpha interpretation, aerender flags, the DOF camera, track mattes, rasterization, trim paths, punch/whip transitions, text animators. It fails on our premium and exact needs: bezier-to-influence mapping, spatial interpolation, particles, Deep Glow settings, glow on white, compositing a character (shadow, light wrap), VO-synced type, colour management. 12 of the 13 sub-2 scores are coverage gaps, not retrieval problems: the 24-source pilot is too small and too generic for these questions.
verdict.transcripts_vs_pages: About even, but they answer different kinds of question. Of the 11 scores of 2, transcripts carried 6 (n04, n07, n11, n17, n18, n23) and pages 5 (n08, n10, n12, n21, n24). Pages win reference questions: dialogs, flags, option lists, expression code. Transcripts win craft/technique questions: easing feel, transition recipes, rig tricks. Transcripts never contain code or exact values: the n06 expression is 'in a Google Doc', and the Top-10 expressions video has no code at all. Use pages for code and transcripts for method. Per source, the Korenman glow page was retrieved 11 times (4 chunks), a magnet for any light/glow/particle query. The 20-chunk Lumetri video (7% of the corpus) was never retrieved.
verdict.caption_noise: Not the main obstacle. An LLM reads unpunctuated auto-captions fine, and auto-captioned videos produced 2s (Olufemii, Manuel, School of Motion, Jake, Bricks). What hurts: (1) mis-heard terms and product names ('post driers'/'he returned abated' for posterizeTime in 69, 'tool crates shapes' 99, 'Illustrator Trader' 321, 'mass path' 123, 'trends positions' 125, 'mobar' for Motion Bro); (2) visual references with no values ('drag this handle here'); (3) sponsor reads and plugs taking chunk space (60, 65, 81, 92, 120, 319/320); (4) steps split across chunk boundaries (121|122, 103|104). Manual-caption videos (Zammit, SternFX, Marriott 'Elevate') read best. Prefer manual-caption videos and videos whose description or blog post carries the code.

retrieval_improvements.change: Make the keyword half actually contribute: in 'all' mode, 120/120 hits had both_retrievers=false and every top-5 scored exactly 1/(60+rank), so hybrid == vector for these long questions. Take a wider candidate pool (e.g. top-20 vector + top-20 'any' BM25), then rerank, instead of raw RRF top-5. 'any' alone is mixed: it gains n02 (104), n07 (183), n21 (271/273), n24 (239) but loses n08 (193, the second half of the code), n13 (95 RSMB), n14 (108/110 DG2).
Expand neighbouring chunks or merge adjacent same-source hits into one passage (±1 chunk, or the whole section for doc tables and code). Answers routinely straddle boundaries.

Per-source diversity (cap or MMR) once adjacent chunks are merged: six questions spent all 5 slots on one source and two more spent 4 on the Korenman page. The freed slots would surface cross-source answers like 104 for n02.

Return an absolute relevance signal (cosine similarity or reranker score) with a no-answer threshold. Today off-topic results look exactly as confident as real ones, so the agent cannot tell the library has nothing.
Do not hard-filter by type; both types produced 2s. Optionally boost pages for 'which setting/flag/option/expression' phrasing and transcripts for 'how do pros / make it feel' phrasing.
Clean chunks at ingest: strip sponsor reads and channel plugs, drop tail fragments, strip doc footers and nav. This was never the primary failure (0 'chunk' causes) but wastes tokens in hits.
